precepts.text: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me. That was a rap lyric, huh? Shame on you. That is in the Bible. It is not Coolio and it is not Tupac. So the valley of the shadow of death is the same darkness that Job spoke about in Job 10:21 and 22. That is the valley he is talking about.
precepts.point: Then said he unto me, Prophesy unto the wind, prophesy, son of man, and say to the wind, Thus saith the Lord God; Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live. So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army. That is the unity Malcolm was talking about. That unity of us standing together, standing as one, in one mind, one understanding, one God, one race, one nation of people. Not divided or split apart. That is the army God is raising up slowly amongst us. An empire within an empire. That is what we are becoming slowly. And do not think eyes are not on us. Eyes are on us outside of here, and eyes are on us in here too.

note.label: Foundational Babylonian Advocates: Division Among the Dispersion

precepts.why:
Ezekiel was set down “in the midst of the valley which was full of bones”, and they were “very dry.” A valley full of bones is a graveyard. Very dry means no nourishment, no understanding, no water. David names that same valley: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.”

That was a rap lyric, huh? Shame on you. That is in the Bible. It is not Coolio and it is not Tupac. The world took the words of the famous Christian prayer and made a song of them, but the valley of the shadow of death is a real place in the scripture.

It is the same darkness Job spoke about in Job 10:21 and 22. It is the same land Baruch spoke of earlier, where our people wax old and are defiled with the dead in a strange land. And it is the same place Isaiah speaks of when the Lord comes to bring out “them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.” The valley of dry bones, the valley of the shadow of death, the land of darkness and the prison house are all one place: the lands of our captivity.

So the valley Ezekiel walked round about is where our people are today, dead and dry in a strange land. Yet even there the one who walks with the Lord fears no evil, because the Lord is with him, and it is the Lord who will bring those bones to life.

precepts.text: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies. The table is the Bible. Habakkuk 2:2, write the vision and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it; Isaiah 30:8, write it before them in a table and note it in a book for the time to come, that this is a rebellious people. We read the tables about what is happening overseas as entertainment while our own spirit is rotten. You are in the greatest place on earth, being taught the future out of these pages, and some of you scorn it.
precepts.point: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man; God will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able, but will with the temptation make a way to escape. If you understand the joy of the elect you embrace the temptation, because he has your back. He wants you to make it, though there are those appointed to die. Nobody wanted to pay a landlord who tripled the rent in Brooklyn after counting heads across the street; that trial forced us to pool the real estate, carpentry, plumbing, and electrical talent the Lord had among us, and then he blessed us with the building in New York despite the detractors. We never took our eyes off the prize. Do not let anyone take your crown.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
God will with the temptation “make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” While we endure the encounters of temptation that are common to us all, even the temptations of our own lusts, the Lord prepares a table for us: “Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.” Why? Because his mercies endure for ever.

The table is the Bible. Habakkuk shows it: “Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables”. Isaiah shows it: “write it before them in a table, and note it in a book”. The tables are what we are supposed to be reading.

But we read the tables and talk about what's going on overseas while our own spirit is rotten. We read it like entertainment instead of changing what is really going on in us.

Brothers and sisters, you are in the greatest place on the planet earth, and some of you don't even realize it. You are getting teaching that tells you what is happening in the future, because we know the future from reading the Bible. And some of you play games, scorn what is brought out, and take this for a joke. The table is prepared in the presence of our enemies; eat from it.

precepts.text: A land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands, which is Jerusalem, our homeland; so laying in green pastures is going into peace.
precepts.point: The green pastures are peace and the beauty of the land: the grass, the cattle, the flowers of the field. It is going into the homeland, the glory of all lands, which is Jerusalem, Israel.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

precepts.why:
“He maketh me to lie down in green pastures”. What are these green pastures? Ezekiel tells of the land the Most High espied for us when he brought us out of Egypt: “In the day that I lifted up mine hand unto them, to bring them forth of the land of Egypt into a land that I had espied for them, flowing with milk and honey, which is the glory of all lands”.

A land flowing with milk and honey, the glory of all lands, which is Jerusalem, our homeland. The green pastures are peace and the beauty of the land: the grass, the cattle, the flowers of the field. So lying down in green pastures is going into peace, going into the homeland, Jerusalem, Israel.

precepts.text: Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron; that is the shadow of death, captivity.
precepts.point: The shadow of death is those bound in affliction and iron. So the valley of the shadow of death is America, the valley of dry bones, the Israelites waking up in the presence of their enemies.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

precepts.why:
“Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil”. The shadow of death is defined here: “Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron”.

The shadow of death is those bound in affliction and iron: captivity. So the valley of the shadow of death is America, the valley of dry bones, the Israelites waking up in the presence of their enemies. Walking through it, we fear no evil, for he is with us, and his rod and his staff comfort us.

precepts.text: Now go, write it before them in a table and note it in a book; the "it" is the words of the Lord, His laws and commandments to get us right.
precepts.point: They claim to be a Christian nation but do the most killings; the Lord says He will reprove them and set them in order before our eyes, giving us the book, the correction and comfort, to rise up as a great army in the presence of our enemies.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

precepts.why:
“Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies”. What is the table? “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever”.

The “it” is the words of the Lord: His laws, statutes and commandments, written in a table and noted in a book to get us right. The table is the word of the Lord written in a book, our correction and our comfort in these last days, prepared before us in the presence of our enemies, the other nations, and more specifically the Edomite nations whose hands are still in America today.

precepts.text: These things hast thou done and I kept silence; but I will reprove thee and set them in order before thine eyes, talking about the other nations.
precepts.point: They claim to be a Christian nation but do the most killings; the Lord says He will reprove them and set them in order before our eyes, giving us the book, the correction and comfort, to rise up as a great army in the presence of our enemies.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

precepts.why:
How does the Most High prepare the table in the presence of the enemy? By setting them in order before our eyes: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.”

This is talking about the other nations. They do heinous things against us: they kill us, shoot us down, imprison us, put drugs in our neighborhoods and call it a "war on drugs" when they mean war on us, the Israelites. They claim to be a Christian nation but do the most killings, and thought the Most High was such an one as themselves.

He kept silence, but He will reprove them and set them in order before our eyes, giving us the book, the correction and the comfort, right in the presence of our enemies.

precepts.text: After three days and a half the spirit of life from God entered into them and they stood upon their feet, and great fear fell upon them which saw them, in the presence of our enemies.
precepts.point: They claim to be a Christian nation but do the most killings; the Lord says He will reprove them and set them in order before our eyes, giving us the book, the correction and comfort, to rise up as a great army in the presence of our enemies.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

precepts.why:
The table is prepared in the presence of our enemies, and so is the rising: “And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.”

The spirit of life from God enters into them and they stand on their feet, and great fear falls on them which saw them. That is in the presence of our enemies. With the book, the correction and comfort of His laws, statutes and commandments, we rise up as a great army before the very nations that killed us, imprisoned us and put drugs in our neighborhoods.

note.label: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

precepts.why: Here is more detail on who restores. Get to the subject first: “Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.” Elias is Elijah.

note.label: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

precepts.why:
Elijah “wast ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the Lord’s judgment, before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.”

That is “he restoreth my soul”, and that is Christ’s word that Elias truly shall come and restore all things: Elijah restores the tribes of Jacob. That is some beautiful stuff right there.

note.label: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

precepts.why: “Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron.” Being bound in affliction and iron: that is called slavery. That is the valley of the shadow of death. This whole land is the valley of the shadow of death, and wherever our people were made slaves, that is the valley of the shadow of death.

note.label: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

precepts.why: “Though thou hast sore broken us in the place of dragons, and covered us with the shadow of death.” America is the place of dragons. The shadow of death goes with places of affliction and iron, with slavery.

note.label: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

precepts.why: In the New Testament it is the same thing: “To give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.” It is talking about the same thing: them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death are the ones bound in affliction and iron, in the lands of their captivity.

note.label: Gods Memorial: The Smoke of Her Torment

precepts.why:
The Psalm everybody likes reading: “The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul.” This is David speaking, and “he restoreth my soul” is heavy. “He leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.”

“Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death”: the valley of the shadow of death is America. David is in the streets of America, walking. “I will fear no evil”: whatever they bring against him, he does not fear. David is going to be here in the last days, walking in the valley of the shadow of death. That is why the sanctified ones of Isaiah 13 are not just angels: David is one of the sanctified ones.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
“I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.” He’s explaining it: what you read about the shepherd in the book of Psalms, Christ said, that’s me, I’m the good shepherd.

“But he that is an hireling, and not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not”: the sheep, the Israelites, don’t belong to a hireling. He “seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth: and the wolf catcheth them, and scattereth the sheep. The hireling fleeth, because he is an hireling, and careth not for the sheep.”

That’s Christianity, that’s these religious organizations: they’re hirelings, they’re temporary. Even you, once you examine yourself, will determine whether or not you are a hireling in this truth. When we saw a lot of danger around us, the BBC, the SPLC against us, some brothers fled the truth. They saw the wolf coming and they ran for the hills: hirelings. And these ministers, look at them, they got Tyler Perry. Come on with this foolishness.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
Christ comes back again: “I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine. As the Father knoweth me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for the sheep.” Christ said, I lay down my life for the sheep; I’ll give my life for the Israelites.

“And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold”: he said, I got all the sheep, all the Israelites, which are not here in Israel today. “Them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.” Christians will use verse 16 and go, see, other sheep means all nations, every other. No, it ain’t talking about that. Why does it say one fold and one shepherd? Ezekiel 37:22 is the precept.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
This is why it says one fold and one shepherd: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”. The two nations are the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom.

So that’s why Christ said, other sheep I have which are not of this fold. They are not all nations; they are the rest of Israel, brought together under the one shepherd.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: We’re still dealing with the Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want. “Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant”. Our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd: he’s the one in the Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: “And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away.” When the chief Shepherd shall appear: that’s Christ. He is the chief Shepherd.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
“Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock”: he that leads the northern kingdom like a flock. Now you might say that’s just talking about Joseph, or Ephraim. Watch who he’s talking about: “thou that dwellest between the cherubims, shine forth.” That ain’t Joseph dwelling between the cherubims; that’s Christ that dwells between the cherubims.

See, the northern kingdom ain’t forgotten. The Lord ain’t forgot them; he said, I’m going to lead them too. That goes with what we just read: other sheep I have. So he’s going to lead the northern kingdom, Joseph.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
“He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young”. This is what the Lord is going to do.

Start at verse 10: “Behold, the Lord God will come with strong hand, and his arm shall rule for him: behold, his reward is with him, and his work before him.” Then he shall feed his flock like a shepherd. You see that: that’s how gentle the Lord is going to deal with us. Now we know who that shepherd is in Psalms 23:1.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: I shall not lack. “The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame.” Brothers and sisters, understand these are the chief things in life that we all need. We all need water, we all need bread, food, we all need clothing, and an house to cover shame. Those are the four chief principal things that we need in life, and that’s what we shall not want.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: “But godliness with contentment is great gain.” Content with what? Water, food, clothing and shelter. “For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.” You see what it says: food and raiment, the principal things we read earlier in Sirach. Let us be therewith content.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: David said, “I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken”. That’s the righteous: those men and women keeping God’s commandments, involved in the work of God. I said that for a reason. “Nor his seed begging bread.” Why? Because Israel works as a collective, and the Lord will bless us as a collective.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
Working as a collective: “Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold, And laid them down at the apostles’ feet: and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need.”

Those men that distribution was given to, whether they were single or had families, were doing the work. They wasn’t just sitting around asking, got a dollar, got five dollars, and not doing nothing. Those were men involved in God’s work; everybody could speak on their work.

I’m saying that because you always get that one grimy that comes around. He ain’t about nothing, he don’t do nothing, but his hand is always out: I need, I need. What are you doing in this body? Nothing. Have you even paid alms? I don’t have money. I saw you bought liquor last week. Brothers like that can go join them other camps out there. We don’t want you, we don’t need you here, you’re a waste of time. The righteous that are not forsaken, that lack nothing, are those doing God’s work.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee”. That peaceful mind, a peaceful countenance, we all need, by keeping our minds stayed on the Lord. Some of you wake up fighting, you go to sleep fighting, you have a miserable mindset at home.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: “When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.” Putting away childish things: going into sins, youthful lusts. That is part of what it takes to be led to the green pastures and the still waters.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
“Therefore are they before the throne of God, and serve him day and night in his temple: and he that sitteth on the throne shall dwell among them”: that’s Christ. “They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat. For the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters”.

That’s what Psalms 23, that verse 2, was talking about: he leadeth me beside the still waters. “And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes.” Christ is that living fountain of waters.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
Let me give you an example: “But this is a people robbed and spoiled”. We are robbed and spoiled as a people. “They are all of them snared in holes”: we’re snared in religious and political holes. “And they are hid in prison houses”: our people are mass incarcerated. “They are for a prey”: we are for a prey to the nations, “and none delivereth”: nobody delivers the Israelites.

“For a spoil, and none saith, Restore.” Nobody says restore to them what was taken. No nation goes before the U.N., no nation goes before the world court and says, hey, you took their gold, you took their wealth, you took their identity, you took their land, you took their culture, you took their heritage, you took everything: give it back. Not one nation has stood up on our behalf. So I want y’all to see that: and none saith, Restore. Only the Lord can restore our soul.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
What happened to our soul? “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long: and there shall be no might in thine hand.” When it says no might, it means no economic might, no military might, no political might. “The fruit of thy land, and all thy labours”: all our natural resources, “shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up; and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway”. This is why we need to be restored.

Read verse 37 again: “And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.”

And verse 64: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other”: we’re scattered from one side of the earth to the other in slavery. “And there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone”: even a wood cross of Jesus we would serve, and a stone of Islam. This is what it’s talking about.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
I’m explaining in brief what happened to us. “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people”: the nations have taken crafty counsel against us. “And consulted against thy hidden ones”: we are the hidden ones; who we are has been hid in the earth. “They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” See that: they cut us off from being a nation.

“For they have consulted together with one consent”: the nations consulted together with one agreement. “They are confederate against thee”: all the nations are confederate against God’s people, us.

It names the nations. “The tabernacles of Edom”: the white man, that’s the Caucasians. “And the Ishmaelites”: that’s the Arabs. “Of Moab”: Moab is the Chinese. “And the Hagarenes”: the Egyptians. “Gebal”: that’s the Hamites. “And Ammon”: Ammon is the Japanese. “And Amalek”: Amalek, that’s Jewish people; they fall under Esau, Edom, too. “The Philistines”: that’s the Palestinians, “with the inhabitants of Tyre”: those are Hamites. “Assur also is joined with them”: Assur, Syria, Turkey. “They have holpen the children of Lot”: they’re helping Ammon and Moab.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: Now we want to be restored. Watch what the disciples said about being restored, because the church would be like, I know, it’s about everybody being restored. No it ain’t. “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” So restoring the kingdom is only to who? Only to Israel. That’s who’s being restored: only Israel.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: To get there, watch the prophecy. “Why then say the scribes that Elias must first come?” Elias is Elijah. “And Jesus answered and said unto them, Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things.” See what Elijah would do: restore all things. Restore what? Restore our identity to us, restore God’s laws to us.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
“Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments.” Remember the law of Moses, my brothers and sisters. “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet”: here’s the prophecy Christ was making reference to, “before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord”: before Armageddon, before the second coming of Christ.

“And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children”: Elijah would restore your identity, Elijah would restore God’s laws to you, to keep them commandments as the Israelites. “And the heart of the children to their fathers”: we’re the children; Elijah would tell us we are the descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. That’s what Elijah would do. “Lest I come and smite the earth with a curse”: before I destroy this earth.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
Us being here today is evidence that Elijah has come and gone already. Look at verse 4 so we know who it is talking about: “O Elias, how wast thou honoured in thy wondrous deeds! and who may glory like unto thee!”

Then verse 10: “Who wast ordained for reproofs in their times”: that’s God’s laws, reproofs. “To pacify the wrath of the Lord’s judgment, before it brake forth into fury”: only by us keeping God’s laws is the wrath of God’s judgment pacified. “And to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.” That’s some heavy stuff. That’s what Elijah has come and done.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
He restoreth my soul; these are the steps. “And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.”

What’s heavy about that: restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning. You think back and you go, wait a minute, that was Adam and Eve. I’m just going to leave that on the table for another day.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: “And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.” The restorer of paths to dwell in: that’s what we’re doing now, as Elijah has come and gone, brothers and sisters. Our mission is to restore the paths to dwell in.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: “For I will restore health unto thee”: everybody’s sick and ailing, and he said, don’t worry about that, I’m going to restore health to thee. “And I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord; because they called thee an Outcast”. Outcast: God is just being nice, but that’s what it’s talking about. “Saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after”: this is Zion, that nobody gives a dag on about. So the point is, I will restore health unto thee, I will heal thee of thy wounds.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: “And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her”. Don’t worry about the dead. A lot of times our mind wonders, what about those of us who have died in this truth? Don’t worry about them; they too shall be restored. “And so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed unto them.” So everything’s going to be restored.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: “Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it; let them be driven backward and put to shame that wish me evil.” Many nations, like we read in Psalms 83, have wished us evil, and you even have amongst our own people those that wish us evil. Let them be put to shame, O Lord, that seek after my soul to destroy it.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
“Repent ye therefore, and be converted”: repent ye therefore and be changed. Converted means to be changed to God’s laws. The man you was last year, you should not be that same man this year; the woman you was last year, you should not be the same woman this year. You must be converted according to God’s laws. “That your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord; And he shall send Jesus Christ, which before was preached unto you”: he’s going to send the Lord to save us, deliver us.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

I will fear no evil. “Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing”: he that keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing. “And a wise man’s heart discerneth both time and judgment”: if you’re wise, you will discern time and judgment.

Some of you hang around your drug dealer buddies or your drug user buddies, and if you hang around five drug users you’re going to be the sixth. That’s like the sister with her five girlfriends: give it time, she’ll be the sixth. I ain’t a hoe. You just give it time. You are who your circle of friends are.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:

Jump down to verse 11: “Let not an evil speaker be established in the earth”: the evil speaker is the politicians and their ministers. “Evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him.” Evil’s going to hunt the violent man to overthrow him.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
Still dealing with I will fear no evil. “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life: To keep thee from the evil woman, from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman.” You didn’t know some women is evil, did you? Some of you brothers been through a horrendous divorce. You had homes and houses and cars, and now you are living in your mama’s basement because you met that good looking, big booty, big breasted evil woman.

You might be skin and bones, she’ll make you think you look like Arnold Schwarzenegger. And she will fool you and get everything you got, and then you are crushed and destroyed.

Time went by and she took the money out of his bank account, got into his VA benefits, put her name on it, changed the code and blocked him out and got all the funds. He went back with the woman anyway, and then he found her diary and found out she been sleeping with everybody. Now he’s doing videos cursing us out, rather than saying, brother, y’all was right. All we did was warn you. I’ve seen this movie before. When your spiritual eyes are open you can discern time and judgment: this is going to happen, brother, here are the signs. Brother, you weak and you are simple. You’re simple as hell. So women can be evil.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
There’s a woman online talking about men could be evil too. Yeah they can, but we ain’t talking about that right now; don’t change the subject. “And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.” The men started to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. “And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods”: the men started to worship their gods. “And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.” The Lord was mad with us.

“And the Lord said unto Moses, Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel.” So God told Moses, kill everybody that did this thing; kill them all.

“And Moses said unto the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal–peor.” Did God say, I will restore your judges as at the first? Remember that. So if you was the officer of ten and you knew five of your men did this thing, you had to kill them. If you was a captain of a hundred and 98 of your men did this, what you had to do. Under every judge, every officer, captain, you had men unto you, and you had to know the state of the flock of those men.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
That history ain’t over yet. Who did we commit whoredom with? “And Moses was wroth with the officers of the host, with the captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, which came from the battle. And Moses said unto them, Have ye saved all the women alive?” I see a whole lot of women that y’all saved alive.

“Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.” Moses reveals something heavy. Brother, y’all thought the women loved you: no, them women didn’t love you. There was a plot. Balaam said, we cannot overcome the Israelites, but I got a plan: send those women amongst those men, let those women make them believe they are the cream of the crop, the creme de la creme, and these dumb, stupid Israelite men, yeah baby, I got it going on, get them to sin and you can kill them. note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

This is why we’re trying to gear you men up, with your passports, to assist us in traveling. But we’re only going to choose those men who are diligent, loyal, and prove themselves studied in the scriptures, not just any old random do-nothing brother. When they were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, they knew them places, because they traveled there before. note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

That is what it is talking about, but it is from God’s standpoint.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: “Withhold not correction from the child: for if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.” So the rod is used for beatings, for whippings.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: The rod brings tribulation, and there is glory in it: “we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.”

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
An example of the rod: how your earthly father beats you, and how God beats us. “For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.”

“Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us”: that deals with the rod. Those scriptures in Proverbs are your earthly father beating you. “And we gave them reverence”: when your father beat you it was not to destroy you, it was to teach you lessons in life. note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: The staff: a staff is used to uphold you. note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

Still dealing with they comfort me. “Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God.” Speak comfortably to Jerusalem, “and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished”, that her iniquity is pardoned: God has forgiven us. “For she hath received of the Lord’s hand double for all her sins.”

So we are to comfort our people. We are telling them the truth: our warfare is accomplished, Christ died for our sins, our iniquities are wiped away. So now all we have to do is prepare ourselves.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: What is this table? “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever.” Note it in a book: that is the Bible. That is the table it is talking about.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

That is the part wanted: I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes. Read Psalms 23:5 again: “Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies.” That is what Psalms 50 says. He sets them in order before the eyes, before the eyes of our enemies.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

“Mine eye also shall see my desire on mine enemies, and mine ears shall hear my desire of the wicked that rise up against me.” Some of y’all don’t want that. That is why Christians say all the time you have to forgive everybody, forgive and forget. What you are saying is not Bible. That is what the Bible is saying, and that is when your head gets anointed with oil: you start to think on another level. My enemies need to go down, they need to be destroyed, today God, today destroy them. You have to send them prayers constantly.

Then: “The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree: he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon.”

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

Our forefathers and foremothers cry for that: judge and avenge our blood. That is not taught in church. Nobody teaches that in church, because they say that is not of Jesus. Shut the hell up. That is seeing your desire on your enemies, the anointing of Psalms 92 and Psalms 23.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

That is order, that is discipline, that is honor, that is structure. You don’t say, I’m just going to go see the Lord. You don’t do that.

“That he may dwell in thy courts: we shall be satisfied with the goodness of thy house, even of thy holy temple.”

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
“And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”: come on, Jerusalem. “And their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee”: slavery, oppression, colonialism, loss of identity. “But in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: that is Christ dying on a cross, and this captivity having an end.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together”: the sanctuary is going to be built up, “and I will make the place of my feet glorious.” This is the house of the Lord that Psalms 23 says we will dwell in for ever.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
Back to Isaiah 60:11: “Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night.” Here is the precept, brothers, write this down. “And the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there. And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it. And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.”

So who is written in the Lamb’s book of life? Christians say everybody that believes in white Jesus. Isaiah 4:3 shows whether that is true.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why:
Who is written in the Lamb’s book of life? “And it shall come to pass, that he that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem.” Everyone that is written among the living in Jerusalem.

Back to Revelation 21:27: there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, “but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.” The ones written in the Lamb’s book of life are those written among the living in Jerusalem, not everybody that believes in white Jesus. They are the ones who will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever. So brothers, never give up.

points: The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want. That word "want" means lack.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

points: He maketh me to lie down in green pastures, He leadeth me beside the still waters. Let us look at what these green pastures are.
The green pastures are peace and the beauty of the land: the grass, the cattle, the flowers of the field. It is going into the homeland, the glory of all lands, which is Jerusalem, Israel.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

points: He restoreth my soul and leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for His name's sake.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

points: The valley of the shadow of death is talking about captivity. Though I walk through it I will fear no evil, for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff, they comfort me.
The shadow of death is those bound in affliction and iron. So the valley of the shadow of death is America, the valley of dry bones, the Israelites waking up in the presence of their enemies.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

points: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies. Our enemies are the other nations, but more specifically the Edomite nations whose hands are still in America today.
The table is the word of the Lord: His laws, statutes and commandments written in a book. It is our correction and our comfort in these last days.

He prepares that table in the presence of the enemy by setting them in order before our eyes. The other nations do heinous things against us, they kill us, shoot us down, imprison us, put drugs in our neighborhoods and call it a "war on drugs" when they mean war on us, the Israelites.

They claim to be a Christian nation but do the most killings; the Lord says He will reprove them and set them in order before our eyes, giving us the book, the correction and comfort, to rise up as a great army in the presence of our enemies.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

points: Thou anointest my head with oil, my cup runneth over. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the Lord forever.
We wake up through the words of life, not through the comedic community, not Egyptology, not Scientology, or whatever else is out there.

note.label: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

points: Today’s topic is Buck Breaking and Building God’s People. The Bible teaches us that no broken people is beyond repair.
“He maketh me to lie down in green pastures”: that’s talking about the kingdom, the promised land. “He leadeth me beside the still waters”: the still waters is peace, the word of God.

note.label: Buck Breaking and Building God's People

points: “He restoreth my soul.” Why is that important for today’s lesson? Because in order for our soul to be restored, something catastrophic happened to our soul: it was destroyed. Our mental faculty, our spiritual faculty was decimated through slavery, colonialism and oppression. That caused us to lose our heritage, our culture, our language. We lost everything, brothers and sisters; even our families have been destroyed. Now we’re trying to restore what we’ve lost.
“He leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake”: he leads us in the commandments of God, in the faith of his Son, Christ, for his name’s sake.

note.label: Buck Breaking and Building God's People

points: Remember, Elijah shall truly come and restore all things. “The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want”: he is going to provide. Wherever we lack, he is going to provide for us.

note.label: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

points: “He maketh me to lie down in green pastures”: that is the kingdom. “He leadeth me beside the still waters”: peace in the kingdom.

note.label: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

points: “He restoreth my soul.” Why? Because we would lose our identity, we would lose our heritage. We would forget who we are; we would no longer realize we are the twelve tribes. He would have to restore that, and how? He will send Elijah back, to restore our soul: restore us to who our fathers are, restore us to the commandments that God gave us. That is what Elijah would do. We had to memorize this in church, and nobody could tell you what it means. Your church ain’t teach you that.
“He leadeth me in the paths of righteousness”: that is the commandments, “for his name’s sake.”

note.label: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

points: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death.” It is not a bill you can’t pay or no gas in the car, the way you hear people say it all the time. The valley of the shadow of death is slavery, the lands of our captivity: this whole land, and wherever our people were made slaves. Though I walk through the lands of my captivity, “I will fear no evil: for thou art with me”, for the Lord is with us.

“Thy rod and thy staff they comfort me”: the rod is the Bible. The rod of God is the word of God, and the comfort of God is the word of God. The rod is also for correction, the way you whoop a child, which is taught in the Bible.
So now our children walk in the land of shadows.

note.label: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

points: That Bible breaks up the grip of Christianity. “The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.” David said the Lord is my shepherd. When we think of a shepherd, we visualize in our mind a man with a shepherd’s staff around sheep. But what it’s really talking about is Christ. Christ is the shepherd, we are the sheep. Christ is the king, and we are actually the sheep.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

points: “The Lord is my shepherd”: now we know who that shepherd is. “I shall not want”: I shall not lack. Want means lack, or fall short of.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

points: “He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.” The green pastures and still waters go into the kingdom, first and foremost; the basic answer is leading us to the kingdom. But we’re going to take it down a notch: to get to the kingdom there’s certain things we got to do and apply.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

points: “He restoreth my soul”. What is that implying? We were broken. We were real broken as a people, mentally, spiritually; we were just destroyed as a people. The Lord is the only one that can restore what was taken from us. Only the Lord can restore our soul.

What happened to our soul is the curse: our children given to another people, no might, our labour eaten up, a byword among all nations, scattered, serving wood and stone. The nations took crafty counsel to cut us off from being a nation. Restoring is only for Israel, and these are the steps of it: Elijah first comes and restores all things, our identity and God’s laws; then our judges as at the first, the repairer of the breach, health and healing, the dead raised, and the times of restitution of all things.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

points: “He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.” These are the steps to us being restored: we got to keep these commandments, that’s our righteousness. Christians say Christ led us to Sunday worship, Christ led us to Christmas, to Mother’s Day and Thanksgiving. No he didn’t. Keeping the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus is how he leads us in the paths of righteousness.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

points: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil”. Where and what is this valley? Write this down: the valley, first and foremost, is America and the lands of our captivities. The shadow of death is the darkness we sit in, bound in affliction and iron, spiritually dead in the great city, Babylon the great. The valley full of dry bones is saying the same thing with different words, and the dayspring from on high came to give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death. Psalms, Ezekiel, Revelation and Luke are all saying the same thing.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

points: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil”. Evil comes in many faces, sizes and facets in this world: the nations, the evil man and violent man, the evil woman, our own lust, and our own people who made a covenant with death. Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing. So I will fear no evil has various levels.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

points: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil”. We briefly went over what evil is, in its various forms; now a little more on evil. Remember, the things that occurred before time were written for our learning, because they will occur again. The same people that gathered together against Christ, and against the apostles and the followers of Christ, you think they’re dead and gone: they’re back today.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

points: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil.” We went through in brief some evil plots and plans: mind war, silent weaponry, their plan to destroy blacks and Hispanics. That is their goal, that is their outset. But we have the word of God. “For thou art with me”: the Lord is with us.

“Thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.” When the Bible talks about the rod, it is the rod of correction. The rod is whooping that behind, but from God’s standpoint. The staff is used to uphold you; we call it a cane today. So it is the rod of correction and the staff of support, and they comfort me.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

points: “Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies.” That table is the book, the Bible: God wrote it before them in a table and noted it in a book. And what was written there he sets in order before the eyes, before the eyes of our enemies.

“Thou anointest my head with oil.” When your head gets anointed with oil you start to think on another level: you shall see your desire on your enemies. My enemies need to go down, they need to be destroyed. Christians say you have to forgive everybody; that is not Bible.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

points: “Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever.” It is basically explaining itself, but there is deep understanding in it. Psalms 23 is about dwelling in the house of the Lord: the one the Lord chooses to approach unto him, the Jerusalem he builds up after the captivity, and the city whose gates are never shut, which only those written in the Lamb’s book of life will enter.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

points: I am going to show you God was behind that translation. “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death”: the valley of the shadow of death is America, the land of your captivity. “I will fear no evil: for thou art with me”: God is with us. “Thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.”

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

points: “Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies.” What is that table? The table is the Bible. The Most High is such a mastermind: the white man read the Bible and said, I am going to teach them their own book. The Most High made it so the white man did not change the Bible and did not burn the Bible.

So when it says he prepareth a table before me in the presence of our enemies, which is the so-called white man, it is saying God was behind the Bible being translated and the gathering of the books. Our enemies did not write this book; God prepared this book for us today. When King James had the Hebrew scholars and the brothers that spoke Greek put it together, the Lord was there guiding, making sure it was prepared for us, and he made sure they did not burn or destroy the Bible. Why? Because the prophecy is that after 350 years the spirit of life from God is going to enter into us, we will stand up on our feet, and great fear is going to fall upon them that see us. The prophecy is that we are going to wake up to the truth that we are the Israelites, and we wake up through the Bible.
You could get the Bible anywhere, but the white men were so prideful they said we would never understand this book was talking about us.

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

points: “He maketh me to lie down in green pastures.”

note.label: Escape Christmas Getaway

points: “He restoreth my soul.” To restore your soul is to bring back to remembrance who you are. Without the Bible we would not have known that we are the children of Israel, because all the history books about us have been hidden. God prepared this book for us in the presence of our enemy, and the Lord God says, he restoreth my soul. King James putting the Bible together, the Most High God was behind all of that.
